title: An expanding ring of the hypercompact H II region W 49 N:A2
question: What is the structure and kinematics of the ionized ring in the hypercompact HII region W49N:A2, and what does it imply for how a massive star ends accretion?

what.value: 45 GHz continuum map of W49N:A2 (contours, flux 0.47 Jy)

evidence.quote: This feature was first noted by (cite: DePree2000) in their 45 GHz continuum map

what.value: Ionizing photon luminosity equivalent to O9 ZAMS and ionized gas mass 0.12 Msun

evidence.quote: has the total ionized gas mass of 0.12 M$_\odot$ (cite: DePree2020)

evidence.loc: Expanding ring of ionized gas and its implication
evidence.quote: which should have a mass of 20$\pm$7 M$_\odot$[^4] (cite: Hohle2010)
We assume the distance to W49N to be 11.11$^{+0.79}_{-0.69}$ kpc (cite: Zhang2013)

recipe.method: uvcontsub, then tclean with Briggs weighting; continuum averaged across four windows; cube at 2 km/s
2D Gaussian fits for component size, flux, inclination; double Gaussian fits to profiles for ring size and width
assumptions: Ring is intrinsically circular, tilted, symmetric about polar axis and equatorial plane

recipe.method: Elliptical cross-section model with beta^2 = a^2 cos^2 i + b^2 sin^2 i; 2σ upper limit
assumptions: Ionized gas 10000 K around 20 Msun star for pressure scale height

recipe.method: Gaussian fits to line profiles on PV diagrams along major and minor axes; velocity difference between ridges corrected for inclination 50
assumptions: Minor-axis velocity gives radial motion only; major-axis gives rotation only

recipe.method: Compare with free-fall and Keplerian masses for 20 Msun star; angular momentum conservation to infer origin radius ~170 au

answer_key.quantity: 250 GHz continuum total flux density of A2

evidence.quote: expansion or contraction velocity of 13.2$\pm$1.0 km s$^{-1}$ at the radius of 706 au
rotation velocity of 2.7$\pm$1.0 km s$^{-1}$ at the radius of 642 au

answer_key.quantity: Scale height upper limit 250 GHz / H29α

evidence.quote: The results are $b<$410 au and $b<$ 690 au for the 250 GHz and H29$\alpha$ rings, respectively.

evidence.loc: Expanding ring of ionized gas and its implication

not_stated_but_needed: Which execution blocks were used and how the second set was identified
Exact procedure for double-Gaussian fits to ring profiles and PV slice widths
Rest frequency of H29α used for velocity axis
Details of the 100–450 GHz archival flux measurements
missing_for_reproduction: Fit procedure details for ring widths and PV Gaussians
score_reason: Public data and key tclean settings given, but many imaging and fitting details missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, numeric results, and a moderately complete recipe.
